checkpoint_finding.source_revision_warning: The selected code postdates the GEO releases but carries no admitted biological weights. Project training receipts and sealed chronology determine label exposure.

interpretation: gkm-SVM is a mandatory task-native sequence/accessibility baseline, trained from scratch within crossed donor and genomic folds. It avoids foundation-checkpoint corpus contamination, but it remains highly vulnerable to local leakage through peak calling, background matching, duplicate sequence handling, and fold construction. Its raw score and ALT-minus-REF decision delta describe resemblance to an accessibility-positive class, not a signed target-gene effect.
known_incidents_and_biases: The source repository bundles a historical NFE2H test model and FASTA/prediction fixtures. Those artifacts are software tests only and are prohibited as biological baselines.
The source reader can truncate overlength FASTA records after warning. The adapter must fail before native execution.
Raw decision-value sign depends on the positive/negative label and LIBSVM class ordering; a fixed positive-peak and allele-delta fixture is required.
The project seed affects background sampling and record order; LS-GKM -r is not a general fitting seed.
Thread counts 1, 4, and 16 are implemented separately and can change floating-point reduction order; -T 1 is the frozen reference lane.
Direct gkm-SVM and deltaSVM share the same model weights and are related ablations, not independent evidence.
Accessibility direction does not establish enhancer-gene linkage or the direction of gene expression.
